title: The D-G-E Bridge
kidRule: Right after a short vowel sound, the /j/ sound is usually spelled D-G-E, as in GADGET and FIDGET. After a long vowel or another consonant it is just G-E, as in CAGE and LARGE.
hint: We hear '/j/' right after a short vowel sound, so a quiet letter sneaks in before the G-E. Which one?
reminder: Right after a short vowel sound, '/j/' is spelled D-G-E, with a quiet D in front.

check.question: Why does GADGET have a D before the G-E?
check.correctAnswer: Because the '/j/' sound comes right after a short vowel sound!
distractors: Because every word with G-E in it needs a D
Because the D makes the A say its name

words.def: A small, clever tool or machine that does a special job.
words.sent: This gadget peels an apple in five seconds.
words.story: Nobody knows for sure where this word came from! Sailors were already using it more than a hundred years ago for any little tool whose name they had forgotten.
words.card: Go *get* the *gadget* that butters toast while it sings!

words.def: To keep making little wiggly moves because you cannot sit still.
words.sent: I always fidget when the car ride is long.
words.story: In 2017, little spinning toys made for busy fingers became one of the most popular toys in the world!
words.card: I *get* in trouble when I *fidget* with my peas at dinner!

words.sent: There was a chocolate smudge on his chin.
words.story: Your fingers leave marks on glass because your skin always has a tiny bit of oil and sweat on it!
words.card: The piglet left a *mud* *smudge* on the clean white sofa!

words.def: A strong digging animal with black and white lines on its face.
words.sent: The badger dug a tunnel under the old oak tree.
words.story: This animal's underground home has a special name: it is called a sett!
words.card: The *badger* earned a *badge* for digging the deepest hole!

words.def: A warm, soft breakfast made by cooking oats in milk or water.
words.sent: Goldilocks ate a whole bowl of porridge.
words.story: Scotland holds a world porridge-making contest every year, and the winner takes home the Golden Spurtle. A spurtle is a wooden stick for stirring!
words.card: The bear built a mountain *ridge* out of lumpy *porridge* and skied down it!

words.def: A plan for how much money you have and what you will spend it on.
words.sent: Our budget for the party is twenty dollars.
words.story: This word comes from an old French word for a little leather bag, the kind people once kept their money in!
words.card: My best *bud* spent his whole *budget* on a hat for his goldfish!

words.def: A plump brown bird that lives on the ground and would rather run than fly.
words.sent: A partridge scurried through the tall grass with her chicks.
words.story: In the song 'The Twelve Days of Christmas', the very first gift is a partridge in a pear tree!
words.card: The *partridge* played the *part* of a pear in the school play!

words.def: To knock or push something out of the place where it was stuck.
words.sent: I used a stick to dislodge the ball from the gutter.
words.story: Woodpeckers hammer on tree bark to dislodge the insects hiding underneath, then catch them with a long sticky tongue!
words.card: A moose sneezed so hard that it managed to *dislodge* the roof of the ski *lodge*!

words.def: A small container that you slot into a machine, like the one that holds ink for a printer.
words.sent: Mom put a new ink cartridge in the printer.
words.story: Early video games came on a plastic cartridge that you pushed into the game machine, and lots of kids blew the dust out of it for luck!
words.card: I filled a shopping *cart* with one tiny ink *cartridge* and nine hundred pickles!

words.def: A jumbled mix of many different things.
words.sent: My desk drawer is a hodgepodge of crayons, stickers and string.
words.story: Hodgepodge started out as the name of a stew made by tossing lots of different meats and vegetables into one pot!
words.card: A pea *pod* got lost in a *hodgepodge* of buttons, bells and banana peels!
